description: How solar and batteries exploded while coal stalled — a 27-year visual of global power capacity and storage (2000–2026). Real trends from IEA, BNEF and public energy reports — one technology surges, another gets edged out.
youtube_description:
The Solar Tsunami — a 27-year race showing how solar PV and battery storage went from niche to dominant forces while coal capacity flatlined and began slipping. This visualization threads together data and milestones from IEA, BloombergNEF, national power registries and major policy moments (Paris Agreement, China’s renewables buildouts, record-low solar bids and battery auctions).

Why this matters: by 2022 solar hit ~1 TW of installed capacity — a milestone a decade in the making — and battery energy storage deployments exploded, unlocking solar’s ability to supply firm power. Meanwhile coal, long the backbone of global baseload, stalled and starts to decline in many markets as retirements outpace new builds.

Sources & notes: IEA/BNEF aggregated annual totals and public national capacity reports. Storage numbers are cumulative grid-scale deployments (GWh); solar/wind/coal are cumulative installed capacity (GW). Some 2024–2026 points are conservative industry projections grounded in announced projects and policy pipelines.

If you want a breakdown CSV or the raw numbers for your own chart race, drop a comment. Like, subscribe and hit the bell — we do weekly data visualizations that tell the story behind the numbers.
